detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

With `use_dynamic_bsz=True`, `rearrange_micro_batches` budgets each micro-batch by the sum of its real tokens. On the Megatron BSHD path (`use_remove_padding=False`), however, every micro-batch is stored as `batch_size * aligned_max_seq_len` tokens: it is padded to its longest sequence (or to the mini-batch max with `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`) and then aligned for TP/CP/FP8. A few short samples next to a long one can therefore exceed `max_token_len_per_gpu` by a large factor.

This PR adds an opt-in `megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model=bshd_padded` that budgets the padded storage the BSHD forward actually allocates. The default stays `token`, so behavior is unchanged unless the option is set.

Related: #5338 proposes length-grouped micro-batches for FSDP. This PR differs in three ways: it targets the Megatron BSHD engine, it uses the exact padded length of `preprocess_bshd_engine` (TP/CP/FP8 alignment and `forced_max_seqlen`), and it reuses the existing DP count sync and within-limit loop of `rearrange_micro_batches` (including `min_num_micro_batch` and VPP divisibility) instead of adding a separate code path. It does not include the token hard cap of #6735, and it does not touch the micro-batch construction changed by #7097.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [bshd dynamic](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+bshd+dynamic), [padded token](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+padded+token), [rearrange_micro_batches](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+rearrange_micro_batches). The closest is #5338 (see above). #7519 and #8127 (MXFP8) change THD alignment and #8208 changes BSHD router replay; they may conflict textually but not semantically.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

Run from the repository root on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13):

```bash
RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV=0 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest \
  tests/utils/test_seqlen_balancing_bshd_padded_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_engine_config_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py tests/utils/test_prepare_micro_batches_with_group_size.py \
  tests/special_sanity/test_config_docs.py -q
```

Result: `85 passed, 1 skipped`. The new tests cover:

- `BSHDPadding.num_tokens` equals the tokens allocated by the real `preprocess_bshd_engine` (with stubbed Megatron parallel state) across 36 combinations of TP/CP/FP8, fixed length and sequence length.
- 33+33 tokens with CP=8 cost 96 (aligned), not 66.
- For a mixed short/long batch, the token model packs 16 samples into one micro-batch (16 x 1024 padded tokens), while the padded model isolates the long sample.
- For every micro-batch count from the minimum up to the batch size: the exact count is returned, partitions are non-empty and within budget, and every sample appears exactly once. FP8 padding also stays within budget.
- Budgeting with a fixed length (`pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max`), fail-fast on an oversized single sample, rejection of `force_group_size > 1`, unchanged token-path output vs `main` for a fixed input, and CP scaling through `prepare_micro_batches`.
- A 3-rank Gloo DP group with different batch sizes and length distributions: every rank gets the same micro-batch count (the max of the local counts) and every partition stays within the padded budget. An oversized sample on one rank raises on all ranks without hanging.

`tests/utils/test_seqlen_balancing.py::test_seqlen_balancing_distributed_params` needs CUDA/NCCL. It is not a CPU test and fails the same way on `main` without CUDA.

Example (64 samples: 60 of 200-2000 tokens and 4 of 14k-16k tokens; TP2/CP4; budget 65536):

| | token model | bshd_padded |
|---|---|---|
| per-micro-batch max length | 2 micro-batches, max 502272 padded tokens | 3 micro-batches, max 65472 |
| `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True` | 2 micro-batches, max 502272 | 16 micro-batches, max 62784 |

Not validated yet: GPU runs with a real Megatron BSHD forward/backward, memory and throughput.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=16384 \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model=bshd_padded \
actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=False
```

The reference model follows the actor setting. The critic uses `critic.megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model`.

```python
from verl.utils.seqlen_balancing import BSHDPadding, rearrange_micro_batches

micro_batches, indices = rearrange_micro_batches(
    batch, max_token_len, dp_group=dp_group, bshd_padding=BSHDPadding(tp_size=2, cp_size=4)
)
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Cost contract: `len(mb) * get_bshd_padded_seq_len(raw_len, len(mb), tp, cp, fp8) <= max_token_len_per_gpu * cp_size`. Here `raw_len` is the micro-batch max, or the mini-batch max when `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`.
- `verl/utils/seqlen_balancing.py`:
  - `get_bshd_padded_seq_len` computes the TP/CP/FP8 alignment and is now shared with `preprocess_bshd_engine`.
  - `BSHDPadding` describes the padding rule.
  - A new partitioner sorts samples by length, cuts greedy contiguous runs under the budget, and splits the most expensive run until the requested count is reached.
  - `rearrange_micro_batches(..., bshd_padding=None)` uses the partitioner for the initial count and inside the existing within-limit loop (`all_reduce MIN`). DP ranks therefore agree on the count, and every partition is checked against the exact padded cost.
  - A single sample whose padded size exceeds the budget fails fast on all ranks through the existing synchronized constraint check.
- `verl/models/mcore/util.py`: `preprocess_bshd_engine` calls the shared alignment helper; behavior is unchanged.
- `verl/workers/engine/utils.py`: `prepare_micro_batches` forwards `bshd_padding`.
- `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: builds `BSHDPadding` from the TP/CP world sizes, `tf_config.fp8` and the `forced_max_seqlen` of `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max`, and rejects `use_remove_padding=True`.
- Config and docs: `McoreEngineConfig.dynamic_bsz_cost_model` (validated), `engine/megatron.yaml`, `ref/megatron_ref.yaml` (follows the actor), the regenerated `_generated_ppo_megatron_trainer.yaml`, and `docs/perf/perf_tuning.rst`.
- Explicitly rejected combinations: THD (`use_remove_padding=True`, which also covers dynamic CP) and `force_group_size > 1`.
- Known approximations:
  - With FP8 padding the alignment depends on the micro-batch size, so the count may exceed the minimum; partitions always stay within budget.
  - VLM BSHD inputs are aligned without FP8, so the cost is an upper bound on that path.

#### Open questions for reviewers

1. With the default `pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`, every micro-batch costs the mini-batch max length, so the count can grow a lot (16 in the example). The docs recommend `False`. Should `bshd_padded` turn it off automatically instead?
2. `bshd_padded` with `use_dynamic_bsz=False` is a documented no-op. Should it raise instead?
3. The option lives in `megatron.*` because only the Megatron BSHD engine needs it, and actor training and log-prob computation share one engine config.

AI assistance (Cursor) was used to write the code, tests and this description. This is a draft: the submitter is reviewing every changed line and will mark it ready after that review.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks: `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passed all hooks.
- [x] Add / Update the documentation: `docs/perf/perf_tuning.rst` and the config comments.
- [x] Add unit tests: the new `*_on_cpu.py` tests are collected by `cpu_unit_tests.yml`. GPU end-to-end validation with Megatron BSHD is still pending.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.
- [x] Not related to the `recipe` submodule.

@@ -172,6 +172,28 @@ Here're some tips to tune the above parameters:
    
 .. :math:`\text{critic.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu}  = 2 \times  \text{actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu})`.
 
+Padded-token budget for Megatron BSHD
+"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""
+
+By default the token limits above bound the real (unpadded) tokens of each micro-batch. On the Megatron BSHD path
+(``use_remove_padding=False``) every micro-batch is stored padded to its longest sequence, so a micro-batch of many
+short samples and one long sample can use far more memory than the limit suggests. Set
+``actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model=bshd_padded`` (the reference model follows the actor;
+``critic.megatron.dynamic_bsz_cost_model`` for the critic) to bound the padded storage instead:
+
+.. code-block:: text
+
+   batch_size * align(seq_len) / context_parallel_size <= max_token_len_per_gpu
+
+``seq_len`` is the longest sequence of the micro-batch, or the longest sequence of the mini-batch when
+``megatron.pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=True`` (the default). In the latter case every micro-batch holds at most
+``max_token_len_per_gpu * cp_size / align(seq_len)`` samples; set ``pad_bshd_to_minibatch_max=False`` to let short
+samples share larger micro-batches. ``align`` is the padding that the BSHD forward applies:
+a multiple of ``tp_size * cp_size * 2`` (``tp_size`` without context parallelism), plus the FP8 block-quantization
+padding when FP8 (``e4m3`` or ``hybrid``) is enabled. Samples of similar length are grouped together, all
+data-parallel ranks use the same number of micro-batches, and a sample that does not fit the limit on its own raises
+an error. It requires ``use_remove_padding=False`` and only takes effect with ``use_dynamic_bsz=True``.
+
 Ulysses Sequence Parallel for Long Context Training
 ----------------------------------------------------

+"""Dynamic batching with the BSHD padded-token cost model."""
+
+import importlib.util
+import random
+import sys
+import types
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+from tensordict import TensorDict
+
+import verl.utils.device as device_module
+import verl.utils.seqlen_balancing as seqlen_balancing
+from verl.utils import tensordict_utils as tu
+from verl.utils.seqlen_balancing import BSHDPadding, rearrange_micro_batches
+from verl.workers.engine.utils import prepare_micro_batches
+
+
+def _make_batch(seq_lens: list[int]) -> TensorDict:
+    # The Megatron engine feeds jagged input_ids; each row holds its sample index.
+    return tu.get_tensordict(
+        {"input_ids": tu.nested_tensor_from_tensor_list([torch.full((n,), i) for i, n in enumerate(seq_lens)])}
+    )
+
+
+def _padded_tokens(partition: list[int], seq_lens: list[int], bshd_padding: BSHDPadding) -> int:
+    return bshd_padding.num_tokens(len(partition), max(seq_lens[idx] for idx in partition))
+
+
+def _check_partitions(
+    micro_batches: list[TensorDict],
+    partitions: list[list[int]],
+    seq_lens: list[int],
+    max_token_len: int,
+    bshd_padding: BSHDPadding,
+) -> None:
+    assert sorted(idx for partition in partitions for idx in partition) == list(range(len(seq_lens)))
+    for micro_batch, partition in zip(micro_batches, partitions, strict=True):
+        assert partition
+        assert _padded_tokens(partition, seq_lens, bshd_padding) <= max_token_len
+        assert [int(row[0]) for row in micro_batch["input_ids"].unbind()] == partition
+
+
+def _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch, tp_size: int, cp_size: int):
+    parallel_state = types.ModuleType("megatron.core.parallel_state")
+    parallel_state.get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size = lambda: tp_size
+    parallel_state.get_context_parallel_world_size = lambda: cp_size
+    parallel_state.get_context_parallel_rank = lambda: 0
+    packed_seq_params = types.ModuleType("megatron.core.packed_seq_params")
+    packed_seq_params.PackedSeqParams = type("PackedSeqParams", (), {"__init__": lambda self, **kwargs: None})
+    core = types.ModuleType("megatron.core")
+    core.parallel_state = parallel_state
+    megatron = types.ModuleType("megatron")
+    megatron.core = core
+    for name, module in {
+        "megatron": megatron,
+        "megatron.core": core,
+        "megatron.core.parallel_state": parallel_state,
+        "megatron.core.packed_seq_params": packed_seq_params,
+    }.items():
+        monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, name, module)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(device_module, "is_npu_available", False)
+
+    util_path = Path(__file__).parents[2] / "verl" / "models" / "mcore" / "util.py"
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("mcore_util_bshd_padding", util_path)
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("tp_size", "cp_size", "use_fp8_padding"),
+    [(1, 1, False), (4, 1, False), (1, 8, False), (2, 2, False), (1, 1, True), (2, 2, True)],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_lens", [[33, 33], [1, 7, 100], [129, 3, 64, 5, 17]])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fixed_seq_len", [None, 150])
+def test_num_tokens_matches_preprocess_bshd_engine_allocation(
+    monkeypatch, tp_size, cp_size, use_fp8_padding, seq_lens, fixed_seq_len
+):
+    mcore_util = _load_mcore_util_with_stubbed_megatron(monkeypatch, tp_size=tp_size, cp_size=cp_size)
+    input_ids = tu.nested_tensor_from_tensor_list([torch.ones(n, dtype=torch.long) for n in seq_lens])
+
+    input_ids_bshd, _, _ = mcore_util.preprocess_bshd_engine(
+        input_ids, use_fp8_padding=use_fp8_padding, forced_max_seqlen=fixed_seq_len
+    )
+
+    # Each CP rank holds 1/cp_size of every padded sequence.
+    allocated_tokens = input_ids_bshd.shape[0] * input_ids_bshd.shape[1] * cp_size
+    bshd_padding = BSHDPadding(
+        tp_size=tp_size, cp_size=cp_size, use_fp8_padding=use_fp8_padding, fixed_seq_len=fixed_seq_len
+    )
+    assert bshd_padding.num_tokens(len(seq_lens), max(seq_lens)) == allocated_tokens
+
+
+def test_budget_counts_context_parallel_alignment():
+    seq_lens = [33, 33]
+    # With CP=8 each sequence is padded to a multiple of 16, so the pair stores 2 * 48 = 96 tokens, not 66.
+    bshd_padding = BSHDPadding(cp_size=8)
+
+    micro_batches, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), 95, bshd_padding=bshd_padding)
+    assert len(partitions) == 2
+    _check_partitions(micro_batches, partitions, seq_lens, 95, bshd_padding)
+
+    _, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), 96, bshd_padding=bshd_padding)
+    assert partitions == [[0, 1]]
+
+
+def test_mixed_lengths_pack_differently_from_token_model():
+    seq_lens = [1024] + [64] * 15
+    max_token_len = 2000
+    bshd_padding = BSHDPadding()
+
+    _, token_partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), max_token_len)
+    micro_batches, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), max_token_len, bshd_padding=bshd_padding)
+
+    # 1984 real tokens fit one micro-batch, but BSHD pads all 16 samples to 1024 tokens each.
+    assert token_partitions == [list(range(16))]
+    assert _padded_tokens(token_partitions[0], seq_lens, bshd_padding) == 16 * 1024
+    _check_partitions(micro_batches, partitions, seq_lens, max_token_len, bshd_padding)
+    assert sorted(partitions) == [[0], list(range(1, 16))]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bshd_padding", [BSHDPadding(), BSHDPadding(tp_size=2, cp_size=2)])
+def test_every_feasible_micro_batch_count_is_valid(bshd_padding):
+    rng = random.Random(0)
+    seq_lens = [rng.randint(1, 300) for _ in range(24)]
+    max_token_len = 1024
+    _, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), max_token_len, bshd_padding=bshd_padding)
+    min_count = len(partitions)
+
+    for num_micro_batches in range(min_count, len(seq_lens) + 1):
+        micro_batches, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(
+            _make_batch(seq_lens), max_token_len, min_num_micro_batch=num_micro_batches, bshd_padding=bshd_padding
+        )
+        assert len(partitions) == num_micro_batches
+        _check_partitions(micro_batches, partitions, seq_lens, max_token_len, bshd_padding)
+
+
+def test_fp8_padding_partitions_stay_within_budget():
+    rng = random.Random(1)
+    seq_lens = [rng.randint(1, 200) for _ in range(16)]
+    max_token_len = 1024
+    bshd_padding = BSHDPadding(tp_size=2, use_fp8_padding=True)
+
+    for num_micro_batches in range(1, len(seq_lens) + 1):
+        micro_batches, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(
+            _make_batch(seq_lens), max_token_len, min_num_micro_batch=num_micro_batches, bshd_padding=bshd_padding
+        )
+        assert len(partitions) >= num_micro_batches
+        _check_partitions(micro_batches, partitions, seq_lens, max_token_len, bshd_padding)
+
+
+def test_fixed_seq_len_budgets_every_micro_batch_at_that_length():
+    seq_lens = [100, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10]
+    max_token_len = 250
+
+    _, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), max_token_len, bshd_padding=BSHDPadding())
+    assert len(partitions) == 2
+
+    bshd_padding = BSHDPadding(fixed_seq_len=100)
+    micro_batches, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), max_token_len, bshd_padding=bshd_padding)
+    assert len(partitions) == 3
+    _check_partitions(micro_batches, partitions, seq_lens, max_token_len, bshd_padding)
+
+
+def test_single_sample_exceeding_padded_budget_fails_fast():
+    # 33 raw tokens fit the budget of 40, but CP=8 pads the sample to 48.
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="single sample takes 48 padded BSHD tokens"):
+        rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch([33, 5]), 40, bshd_padding=BSHDPadding(cp_size=8))
+
+
+def test_rejects_forced_groups():
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="force_group_size"):
+        rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch([4, 4]), 16, force_group_size=2, bshd_padding=BSHDPadding())
+
+
+def test_token_cost_model_is_unchanged():
+    seq_lens = [7, 3, 9, 2, 5, 8, 1, 6, 4, 10]
+
+    _, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), 20)
+    assert partitions == [[1, 2, 7], [3, 4, 5, 8], [0, 6, 9]]
+    _, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), 20, min_num_micro_batch=4)
+    assert partitions == [[1, 9], [0, 3, 7], [4, 5, 6], [2, 8]]
+
+
+def test_prepare_micro_batches_budgets_padded_tokens_per_gpu():
+    seq_lens = [33, 33, 20, 3]
+    data = _make_batch(seq_lens)
+    # The Megatron engine scales the per-GPU budget by the CP size, as each CP rank stores 1/cp of a sequence.
+    tu.assign_non_tensor(data, use_dynamic_bsz=True, sp_size=8, max_token_len_per_gpu=12)
+    bshd_padding = BSHDPadding(cp_size=8)
+
+    micro_batches, partitions = prepare_micro_batches(data, bshd_padding=bshd_padding)
+
+    _check_partitions(micro_batches, partitions, seq_lens, 96, bshd_padding)
+    assert len(partitions) == 2
+
+
+def _dp_worker(rank: int, world_size: int, init_method: str) -> None:
+    dist.init_process_group(backend="gloo", init_method=init_method, world_size=world_size, rank=rank)
+    seqlen_balancing.get_device_name = lambda: "cpu"
+    rng = random.Random(rank)
+    # Ranks differ in batch size and length distribution, so they need different micro-batch counts on their own.
+    seq_lens = [rng.randint(1, 64) for _ in range(12)] if rank == 0 else [rng.randint(100, 500) for _ in range(9)]
+    if rank == 2:
+        seq_lens += [1000]
+    max_token_len = 1024
+    bshd_padding = BSHDPadding(tp_size=2, cp_size=2)
+
+    micro_batches, partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(
+        _make_batch(seq_lens), max_token_len, dp_group=dist.group.WORLD, bshd_padding=bshd_padding
+    )
+
+    _check_partitions(micro_batches, partitions, seq_lens, max_token_len, bshd_padding)
+    _, local_partitions = rearrange_micro_batches(_make_batch(seq_lens), max_token_len, bshd_padding=bshd_padding)
+    counts = [None] * world_size
+    dist.all_gather_object(counts, (len(local_partitions), len(partitions)))
+    assert len({synced for _, synced in counts}) == 1
+    assert len({local for local, _ in counts}) > 1
+    assert counts[rank][1] == max(local for local, _ in counts)
+
+    # One rank holding an oversized sample must make every rank raise instead of hanging.
+    oversized_seq_lens = [33, 5] if rank == 1 else [5, 5]
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="single sample takes 48 padded BSHD tokens"):
+        rearrange_micro_batches(
+            _make_batch(oversized_seq_lens), 40, dp_group=dist.group.WORLD, bshd_padding=BSHDPadding(cp_size=8)
+        )
+
+    dist.barrier()
+    dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+def test_dp_ranks_agree_on_micro_batch_count_within_padded_budget(tmp_path):
+    world_size = 3
+    init_file = tmp_path / "dist_init"
+    init_file.write_text("")
+    mp.spawn(_dp_worker, args=(world_size, f"file://{init_file}"), nprocs=world_size, join=True)

@@ -44,6 +44,11 @@ def test_offload_flags(self, offload_field):
         config = McoreEngineConfig(**{offload_field: True})
         assert getattr(config, offload_field) is True
 
+    def test_rejects_unknown_dynamic_bsz_cost_model(self):
+        McoreEngineConfig(dynamic_bsz_cost_model="bshd_padded")
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="dynamic_bsz_cost_model"):
+            McoreEngineConfig(dynamic_bsz_cost_model="padded")
+
 
 class TestFSDPEngineConfigCPU:
     def test_default_values(self):

@@ -25,6 +25,7 @@
 from megatron.core.packed_seq_params import PackedSeqParams
 
 from verl.utils.device import is_npu_available
+from verl.utils.seqlen_balancing import get_bshd_padded_seq_len
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__file__)
 logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARN"))

+    max_seq_len: int, batch_size: int, tp_size: int, cp_size: int, use_fp8_padding: bool

+    """Return the sequence length that the Megatron BSHD forward pads a micro-batch to.

+    For CP (zigzag), the sequence length must be divisible by ``2 * cp_size``. After the zigzag CP split each rank

+        tp_size: Tensor model parallel size.

+    runs = [[order[0]]]

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

# Contributor License Agreement (CLA) assistant

Streamline your workflow and let CLA assistant handle the legal side of contributions to a repository for you. CLA assistant enables contributors to sign CLAs from within a pull request.

To get started, simply store your CLA as a GitHub Gist file then link it with the repository/organisation in CLA assistant. Then sit back and relax while CLA assistant:

- Comments on each opened pull request to ask the contributor to sign the CLA
- Allows contributors to sign a CLA from within a pull request
- Authenticates the signee with their GitHub account
- Updates the status of a pull request when the contributor agrees to the CLA
- Automatically asks users to re-sign the CLA for each new pull request in the event the associated Gist & CLA has changed
- Green lights merge queues without additional CLA checks as everyone needs to have signed of on the PR level already

Repository owners can review a list of users who signed the CLA for each version of it. To get started, visit [cla-assistant.io](https://cla-assistant.io).
